title: Person Registry — Pass B adjudications
description: What the registry pass's SECOND LLM call returns (#550, W9r): one verdict per claim in registry_claims.json. This pass is dispatched FRESH and sees only its own instructions and the claims document -- never Pass A's conversation and never registry_verdicts.json -- because the failure it exists to catch is a plausible-and-wrong judgement, and a reader who already holds the narrative that produced it is not an independent check on it. Every entry echoes the claim_id it is judging: a positional list of anonymous booleans could apply an affirmation meant for a safe claim to an unsafe one, and nothing downstream would see it. --build requires an exact one-to-one join -- no missing id, no duplicate id, no id the claims document does not contain. Absence, false, and hedging are treated identically: not affirmed. Lives under assets/schemas/registry/ for the same reason as its siblings -- see registry-verdicts.schema.json's own description.

input_sha256.description: Copied verbatim from registry_claims.json. Binds this document to the same prep bytes Pass A judged.

claims_sha256.description: Copied verbatim from registry_claims.json's own claims_sha256. --build recomputes it from the claims file on disk, so an adjudication set produced against a different projection of a different verdict cannot be consumed.

claim_id.description: The sha256 of the claim's own canonical JSON, as registry_claims.json states it. Deterministic, so it cannot drift between the two documents.

affirmed.description: true only when the evidence in the claim itself establishes it. For a person claim that means these units denote a person, and -- when there is more than one -- the same person. For a typed claim it means the quote STATES that exact relation, place or date between those exact parties; a quote that merely mentions both is not affirmation. For a printed-surface assignment it means the book prints that string for this person. For an identity-status claim it means the identity is genuinely settled rather than merely undisputed-so-far.
